prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Sign-in hints, preset customization fallback flow, sequence reordering, interactive wait flows and tips, and interactive desktop hotkey setup were helpful.
Hints outside sign-in, copy updates, sign-in step reordering, and layout changes showed no clear effect or hurt performance.
Most new screens hurt performance or showed no clear effect, with the exception of interactive desktop hotkey setup.
Predictions were too high for failed, harmful, or no-effect changes, overestimating gains.
Predictions were too low for winning sequence reorderings, interactive waiting flows, and setup screens expected to perform poorly.

Changes:
0: [adoption, new_flow] Interactive Pet Trait Customization Playroom Flow: Adds an interactive trait preview flow to friend selection where users can play test companion behaviors before confirming adoption. (why: Adoption has the highest drop-off rate (37.3% drop) and long decision times (median 89s / mean 1017s); interactive previews increase engagement.)
1: [home, new_screen] Interactive Desktop Pet Activity Stage Screen: Inserts a dedicated interactive pet activity stage screen while background desktop rendering completes. (why: The waiting step takes a median of 201s and mean of 2336s. Interactive wait flows have previously proven highly effective.)
2: [sign_in, reorder] Sign-In Post-Adoption Flow Reorder: Reorders the onboarding journey so account sign-in happens after picking and naming the desktop pet. (why: Moving account creation after pet customization builds attachment first and reduces initial sign-in friction.)
3: [sign_in, hint] Existing Account Pet Sync Reassurance Hint: Adds an explicit sync reassurance hint on the sign-in screen confirming existing pets will be automatically restored. (why: 8 support emails reported lost or reset pets after signing back in.)
4: [home, wait_info] Desktop Engine Initialization Stage Progress Info: Displays breakdown progress stages and estimated completion time during desktop engine loading. (why: Waiting step drop-off occurs during long loading times (mean 2336s). Detailed stage feedback keeps users informed.)
5: [choose_path, hint] Path Story Companion Behavior Callout Hint: Adds an inline path callout hint explaining how story path selection determines companion traits. (why: Choose path has a 20.9% drop-off; setting clear expectations on path benefits encourages progression.)
6: [finish, new_screen] Interactive Desktop Companion Control Tutorial Screen: Adds a dedicated interactive tutorial screen demonstrating how to summon, minimize, and talk to your pet on the desktop. (why: Multiple support emails expressed confusion on how to control or hide their pet after onboarding.)
7: [finish, redesign] Desktop Welcome Interactive Quick-Action Redesign: Redesigns the final home intro screen into a split interactive view with instant companion action buttons. (why: 28.7% of users drop during the final finish step; providing immediate interactive actions increases completion.)

scores.note: Adoption has highest drop-off, but new flows historically fail to improve conversion.
Interactive wait flows work well, though introducing new screens carries extra cost and risk.
Sign-in step reordering has consistently hurt performance in past tests.
Sign-in hints are strongly supported by support emails and past test results.
Progress feedback during wait steps has reliably improved retention.
Hints outside sign-in have shown no meaningful effect in historical data.
Addressing confusion reported in support emails, but new screens at finish heavily drop conversion.
Redesigning existing steps has historically yielded negative relative lift.
